[RCLI.1.12] **`check` gives `compile`'s verdict and writes no artefact.** The
compiler must do everything `compile` does to the input short of writing the
artefact, resolving its imports and dialects as `compile` does. Its exit code,
and what it writes to standard error, are what `compile` gives for the same
input under the same `--diagnostics` ([RCLI.3.2]). The input is a path or `-`,
and `--filename` names it, as [RCLI.1.9] says. It takes no `-o`, and an
invocation naming one is a usage error ([RCLI.3.1]).

With `--dump-ast`, the compiler must write one JSON document to standard output
that validates against `compiler/dsc_check.schema.json`, and nothing to standard
error. The exit code does not move. What the schema cannot carry:

- **`tree` does not wait for the verdict.** It is the tree `dump-ast` writes for
  the input ([RCLI.1.10]) whenever the input parses, a program a later phase
  refuses included, and `null` only when the input does not parse.
- **`diagnostics` is what `compile` would have written to standard error**, in
  the form `--diagnostics` chooses.
